rooms.line: No pressure. I just made extra.

opts.t: Eat a few bites: “Thank you. I really needed that.”
opts.why: Accepting practical help strengthens relationships.
opts.re: I'm so glad. There's more if you want it — no rush.
opts.say: Thank you. I really needed that.

opts.t: “Looks great, leave it and I'll eat once my stomach settles.”
opts.why: Polite deflection leaves you running on empty.
opts.re: Okay… I'll leave it here. Just try a little when you can?
opts.say: Looks great, leave it and I'll eat once my stomach settles.

opts.t: Leave the plate where it is: “Not hungry. Thanks though.”
opts.why: Turning down food you clearly need neglects your body and pushes away care.
opts.re: …It's here if you want it later.

rooms.title: Naming Burden Guilt
rooms.scene: Washing dishes together, guilt suddenly hits.
rooms.line: Hey, you went quiet. What's going on?

opts.t: “I feel like a burden. Can I say that without you trying to fix it?”
opts.why: Saying thoughts out loud lets partners respond.
opts.re: Of course. No fixing. Just listening — and you're not a burden.
opts.say: I feel like a burden. Can I say that without you trying to fix it?

opts.t: “Just zoned out—sorry I haven't been fun lately.”
opts.why: Apologizing hides real guilt.
opts.re: You don't have to be fun. I just want the real you.
opts.say: Just zoned out—sorry I haven't been fun lately.

opts.t: Dry your hands and step back: “Nothing. I'm going to lie down.”
opts.why: Stepping away halts joint activity.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll finish these.

rooms.title: Friend Dropping Off Groceries
rooms.scene: A friend leaves soup on your doorstep.

opts.t: Open door in sweatpants: “Thank you—no energy to host, porch drop-off is a lifesaver.”
opts.why: Accepting help on your terms models boundaries.
opts.re: See? People want to show up for you. I love that.
opts.say: Thank you—no energy to host, porch drop-off is a lifesaver.

opts.t: “Don't spend money on me! Take it home, I have food.”
opts.why: Refusing care out of pride deprives friends of love.
opts.re: They wanted to help… maybe let them?
opts.say: Don't spend money on me! Take it home, I have food.

opts.t: Leave your phone on the table: “I'll reply tomorrow. Or something.”
opts.why: Ignoring delivery notifications leaves friends waiting.
opts.re: …Your friend texted. Did you see?

rooms.title: Delegating at Work
rooms.scene: You're drowning in work deadlines with brain fog.

opts.t: Message manager early: “Hitting bandwidth overload—can we prioritize top two and push rest?”
opts.why: Communicating limits protects wellbeing.
opts.re: That's really brave. You're protecting yourself — good.
opts.say: Hitting bandwidth overload—can we prioritize top two and push rest?

opts.t: Keep quiet and grind: “I'll just work till midnight. Nobody needs to know I'm struggling.”
opts.why: Suffering in silence prevents adjustments.
opts.re: Please don't run yourself into the ground tonight.

opts.t: Minimize the window: “I'll deal with it later. Or never.”
opts.why: Hiding applications sidesteps communication.
opts.re: …Everything okay over there?

rooms.title: Letting Someone Hold Space
rooms.scene: {P} sits quietly beside you on the couch while you're drained.

opts.t: Lean back: “Thanks for hanging out quietly—it helps a lot.”
opts.why: Realizing you needn't perform relieves social pressure.
opts.re: No need to perform. I'm happy just being here with you.
opts.say: Thanks for hanging out quietly—it helps a lot.

opts.t: Keep the conversation going: “So—how was your day? And your week? Anything new?”
opts.why: Overcompensating drains reserves.
opts.re: You don't have to entertain me. Just rest.

opts.t: Shift away a little: “You don't have to babysit me, you know.”
opts.why: Shifting physical distance creates unspoken space.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll give you some space.

rooms.title: Saying Yes to Rides
rooms.scene: {P} offers to drive you to your appointment.

opts.t: “I'd appreciate that—riding passenger sounds easier today.”
opts.why: Sharing logistics conserves energy.
opts.re: Passenger seat's all yours. Happy to.
opts.say: I'd appreciate that—riding passenger sounds easier today.

opts.t: “No, I'll take two buses—don't want to inconvenience you.”
opts.why: Choosing hardship prolongs exhaustion.
opts.re: It's really no trouble. The offer stands.
opts.say: No, I'll take two buses—don't want to inconvenience you.

opts.t: Put your shoes back: “Actually, I might just skip it today.”
opts.why: Skipping the appointment instead of accepting the ride cuts you off from help.
opts.re: …Oh. Okay, next time then.

rooms.title: Accepting a Check-In Call
rooms.scene: Your sibling calls; you have very low energy.

opts.t: Answer warmly: “Super low-battery today so I have five minutes, but glad to hear you.”
opts.why: Setting time boundaries protects energy.
opts.re: Five minutes of love counts. Good call.
opts.say: Super low-battery today so I have five minutes, but glad to hear you.

opts.t: Stay on the line: “No, no, I'm not busy—tell me everything!”
opts.why: Ignoring limits drains energy.
opts.re: You look wiped… it's okay to hang up, you know.

opts.t: Watch it ring out: “I'll call back when I'm normal again.”
opts.why: Allowing calls to ring bypasses connection.
opts.re: …Was that your sibling? They'll worry.

rooms.title: Sharing Household Load
rooms.scene: You watch {p} start cooking dinner.

opts.t: Offer one tiny contribution: “I can sit at the table and chop vegetables.”
opts.why: Contributing within capacity preserves partnership.
opts.re: Perfect. Chopping buddy. I love this.
opts.say: I can sit at the table and chop vegetables.

opts.t: Take over the stove: “Move over, I'll make the whole thing myself. I owe you.”
opts.why: Overriding limits leads to frustration.
opts.re: Hey, sit — you don't have to prove anything to me.

opts.t: Sit and watch: “I'd only get in the way.”
opts.why: Deciding you'd only be in the way keeps you on the sidelines of your own home.
opts.re: …Want to keep me company at least?

rooms.title: Asking for Reassurance Directly
rooms.scene: You wake up feeling insecure.
rooms.ask: What is the cleanest way to ask for comfort?

opts.t: Ask directly: “Nasty thoughts right now—could I get a hug and hear we're okay?”
opts.why: Asking clearly is healthy communication.
opts.re: Come here. We're okay. We really are.
opts.say: Nasty thoughts right now—could I get a hug and hear we're okay?

opts.t: Fish for comfort: “Do you think I've been doing okay lately? Be honest…”
opts.why: Indirect testing leaves needs unmet.
opts.re: …You're doing great. But are you okay?

opts.t: Pull the duvet up: “I'm fine. Go back to sleep.”
opts.why: Covering yourself seals off comfort access.
opts.re: …Hey. I'm here if you want a hug.

rooms.title: Receiving a Compliment
rooms.scene: {P} compliments you on how hard you've been trying.

opts.t: Pause: “Thank you. It was really hard, I appreciate you saying that.”
opts.why: Receiving kindness builds self-worth.
opts.re: You earned every word of it. I mean it.
opts.say: Thank you. It was really hard, I appreciate you saying that.

opts.t: Deflect: “I barely did anything, you deserve the credit.”
opts.why: Reflexively erasing effort blocks wins.
opts.re: Don't shrink it — you worked really hard.
opts.say: I barely did anything, you deserve the credit.

opts.t: Look down at your mug: “Not really. Anyone could have done it.”
opts.why: Gazing into mugs deflects praise.
opts.re: …I meant it, you know.

rooms.title: Saying it out loud
rooms.scene: It's midnight and you're still rewriting emails. {P} brings you tea.

opts.t: Close laptop: “I don't know where to start. Everything feels heavy.”
opts.why: Describing feelings messily helps understanding.
opts.re: Then don't start anywhere. Just tell me how heavy it feels.
opts.say: I don't know where to start. Everything feels heavy.

opts.t: “Brain fogged on one paragraph—once I hit send, I'll switch off.”
opts.why: Hyper-focusing on tasks avoids heavier weight.
opts.re: Okay… but this isn't really about one paragraph, is it?
opts.say: Brain fogged on one paragraph—once I hit send, I'll switch off.

opts.t: Stir your tea: “Thanks. I've just got a lot to finish.”
opts.why: Stirring beverages avoids check-ins.
opts.re: …I'll leave the tea here.

rooms.title: Using the Notebook
rooms.scene: The notebook {p} gave you sits on your desk.

opts.t: Open it and write: “Okay. Three honest lines about how I really feel.”
opts.why: Writing feelings down makes them clearer.
opts.re: Three honest lines. That's brave. Thank you for trying.

opts.t: Use it for tomorrow's tasks: “I'll just make a clean priority list. That's more useful.”
opts.why: Structuring tasks sidesteps emotions.
opts.re: A list helps… maybe one line about how you feel, too?

opts.t: Close the notebook: “Writing it down won't change anything.”
opts.why: Snapping journals shut declines expression.
opts.re: …It's yours, whenever you're ready.

rooms.title: Voice Memo When Words Fail
rooms.scene: Your throat feels too tight to talk tonight.
rooms.ask: How do you bridge the gap?

opts.t: Send voice note: “Talking is hard tonight, wrote three sentences.”
opts.why: Asynchronous communication lowers pressure.
opts.re: I got your voice note. Thank you. I'm coming to sit with you.
opts.say: Talking is hard tonight, wrote three sentences.

opts.t: Put it off: “I'll wait until talking feels easier. Maybe in a couple of weeks.”
opts.why: Waiting for zero fear means silence.
opts.re: You don't have to wait. Text me even one word.

opts.t: Lock your phone: “Nobody wants to hear this at night anyway.”
opts.why: Pressing side buttons aborts communication.
opts.re: …Are you still up? I'm here.

rooms.title: Telling a Close Friend
rooms.scene: Your best friend messages: “Haven't heard from you in ages. Coffee this week?”

opts.t: Type honestly: “I'd love that. Heads up—I've been going through a rough time with my mood. Can we keep it low-key?”
opts.why: Letting a trusted friend in, on your own terms, widens your support beyond one person.
opts.re: You told your friend? I'm really glad. You deserve more people in your corner.

opts.t: “Sure! Things are great, just super busy lately!”
opts.why: Agreeing to meet is good, but pretending everything's fine keeps you lonely even in company.
opts.re: …You said things are great? You don't have to pretend with them.

opts.t: “Can't this week, sorry. Maybe next month.”
opts.why: Pushing friends away keeps you isolated, which makes low mood heavier.
opts.re: …You turned down coffee again? Maybe a short one would help.

rooms.title: Describing It
rooms.scene: {P} sits beside you, gentle and curious.
rooms.line: Can you tell me what it actually feels like? I want to understand.

opts.t: Try to put it into words: “It's like everything is behind fog. I'm tired all the time, and nothing feels good anymore.”
opts.why: Describing the feeling, even imperfectly, helps someone understand how to help.
opts.re: …Fog. Okay. Thank you for telling me. That helps me so much.

opts.t: “It's hard to explain. Just stressful, I guess. Work stuff.”
opts.why: Shrinking it to 'work stress' keeps them guessing about what you really need.
opts.re: Work stuff? I feel like it's more than that.

opts.t: “You wouldn't get it. Nobody does.”
opts.why: Deciding they can't understand shuts down someone who's trying.
opts.re: …I'd like to try, if you ever let me.

rooms.title: When a Comment Stings
rooms.scene: A friend makes a clumsy comment about how you're doing.

opts.t: “Thanks—taking it day by day, honestly, but glad to see you.”
opts.why: Correcting gently preserves authenticity.
opts.re: That was honest and kind. Day by day is perfect.
opts.say: Thanks—taking it day by day, honestly, but glad to see you.

opts.t: Smile brightly: “Oh, I'm totally better now! Fully back to normal.”
opts.why: Performing full recovery creates exhausting pressure.
opts.re: You don't have to pretend you're cured for anyone.

opts.t: Adjust your bag strap: “Yeah. Sure.”
opts.why: A flat “yeah, sure” accepts the hurtful comment without protecting yourself.
opts.re: …That comment bugged you, huh?

rooms.title: Keep-Close Reminder
rooms.scene: It's a clear, calm afternoon.

opts.t: Write a note for future you: “What helped, who to text, and: the fog always passes.”
opts.why: Clear-headed breadcrumbs turn past survival into anchors.
opts.re: That note is going to help you so much one day.

opts.t: Push the thought away: “Let's not think about bad days. I don't want to jinx it.”
opts.why: Avoiding preparedness leaves you empty-handed.
opts.re: Bad days might come, but being ready helps.

opts.t: Close the journal: “I don't want to remember any of it.”
opts.why: Closing blank journals misses strategy windows.
opts.re: …Want to write something together?

rooms.title: Low-Energy Comfort Menu
rooms.scene: You're blanking on what usually soothes you.

opts.t: Grab a sticky note: “Three easy comforts: a warm shower, my blanket, rain sounds.”
opts.why: Pre-deciding options removes decision fatigue.
opts.re: That's such a good idea. Want me to add one?

opts.t: Write a full schedule: “Self-care at 7, 8, 9 and 10—every hour, no skipping.”
opts.why: Rigid routines feel like punishment.
opts.re: A schedule? Maybe start with just three easy things.

opts.t: Put the pen back: “Nothing helps anyway.”
opts.why: Returning writing tools bypasses preparation.
opts.re: …Need anything?

rooms.title: Laughing Without Guilt
rooms.scene: You laugh at a funny video, then an impostor thought hits.

opts.t: “Moment of lightness doesn't erase struggle—allowed brief relief.”
opts.why: Understanding depression isn't 24/7 misery stops policing joy.
opts.re: Laugh all you want. It's allowed. I love hearing it.
opts.say: Moment of lightness doesn't erase struggle—allowed brief relief.

opts.t: Stop the video: “I shouldn't be laughing. I'm supposed to be struggling.”
opts.why: Believing you must look miserable traps you.
opts.re: Hey, it's okay to enjoy things. Really.

opts.t: Lock your phone: “Don't get used to it.”
opts.why: Abrupt termination reinforces self-policing.
opts.re: …Was it funny? You stopped so fast.

rooms.title: Sharing Credit With Yourself
rooms.scene: You reflect on how far you've come.

opts.t: “Had support, and did real hard work to get here.”
opts.why: Owning active roles builds confidence.
opts.re: You did the hard work. I'm so proud of you.
opts.say: Had support, and did real hard work to get here.

opts.t: “Just got lucky things calmed down.”
opts.why: Attributing resilience to luck leaves you powerless.
opts.re: It wasn't luck. You worked so hard for this.
opts.say: Just got lucky things calmed down.

opts.t: Look out the window: “I didn't really do anything. It just got easier.”
opts.why: Saying you didn't do anything erases your own hard work.
opts.re: …You've come so far, you know.

rooms.title: Reaching out for real help
rooms.scene: You've felt low for weeks.

opts.t: “Okay. I'm scared, but… can you help me book it?”
opts.why: Saying yes while scared is brave.
opts.re: I'll help you book it. Scared and brave can happen together.
opts.say: Okay. I'm scared, but… can you help me book it?

opts.t: “Let me try fixing sleep first, and if stuck next month I'll book.”
opts.why: Setting conditions delays early intervention.
opts.re: Okay… but please don't wait too long. I'm here.
opts.say: Let me try fixing sleep first, and if stuck next month I'll book.

opts.t: Step back inside: “It's not that bad. Other people have it worse.”
opts.why: Stepping indoors closes the threshold.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll be inside if you change your mind.

rooms.title: Night Before First Appointment
rooms.scene: It's the night before your first appointment, and you can't stop pacing.

opts.t: “Terrified. What if they think I'm weak? Can you remind me why?”
opts.why: Sharing fear lets someone reassure you.
opts.re: Because you deserve to feel better. That's brave, not weak.
opts.say: Terrified. What if they think I'm weak? Can you remind me why?

opts.t: “Keep this strictly between us so nobody treats me differently.”
opts.why: Treating therapy as shameful hurts commitment.
opts.re: It's yours to share… but there's nothing shameful here.
opts.say: Keep this strictly between us so nobody treats me differently.

opts.t: Walk past: “I don't want to talk about tomorrow.”
opts.why: Pacing past avoids verbal processing.
opts.re: …Hey. I'm nervous for you too.

rooms.title: Clinic Waiting Room
rooms.scene: You're sitting in the clinic waiting room, fighting the urge to leave.
rooms.ask: How do you ride out the urge?

opts.t: Breathe: “I don't have to spill everything—just stay ten minutes.”
opts.why: Breaking courage into tiny increments helps.
opts.re: Ten minutes. You can do ten minutes. I'm proud of you.
opts.say: I don't have to spill everything—just stay ten minutes.

opts.t: Write a cancellation email, just in case: “If it gets too much, I'll just send this.”
opts.why: Keeping escape hatches open feeds anxiety.
opts.re: Maybe don't send it… just see how it goes?

opts.t: Watch the clock: “This was a mistake. I should just go.”
opts.why: Fixating on clock ticks internalizes distress.
opts.re: …You okay? You can text me anytime.

rooms.title: The Waitlist
rooms.scene: The counseling center says the next opening is in six weeks.

opts.t: Join the waitlist and ask: “Is there anything sooner—your doctor, a cancellation list, or a support line meanwhile?”
opts.why: Asking about other options keeps help moving while you wait.
opts.re: Six weeks, but you found other options? That's really smart.

opts.t: Take the slot and decide: “I'll just white-knuckle it till then.”
opts.why: Getting on the list is good, but going it alone for six weeks is hard on you.
opts.re: Six weeks is long… lean on me in the meantime, okay?

opts.t: Hang up: “Six weeks? Forget it. Clearly I'm not meant to get help.”
opts.why: Giving up after one obstacle cuts you off from help that's still within reach.
opts.re: …Can I help you call somewhere else?

rooms.title: Telling Your Manager
rooms.scene: You need time off for appointments, but you're dreading the conversation with your manager.

opts.t: Keep it simple: “I'm dealing with a health issue and need a few appointments. Can we plan around them?”
opts.why: Sharing only what you need to protects your privacy and gets you the time for care.
opts.re: You asked for the time off? I'm proud of you. That wasn't easy.

opts.t: Book appointments at lunch only: “I'll squeeze them in so nobody notices.”
opts.why: Hiding care around your job adds stress and makes appointments easier to skip.
opts.re: Rushing to appointments on your lunch break sounds exhausting.

opts.t: “I'll just skip therapy until work calms down.”
opts.why: Putting your health on hold for work usually means it never comes first.
opts.re: Work will never calm down. You matter more than a deadline.

rooms.title: Therapy Office Blankness
rooms.scene: In the therapy office, your mind suddenly goes blank.

opts.t: “Mind went blank—just felt exhausted and empty for weeks.”
opts.why: Therapists expect blankness; naming it helps.
opts.re: That's exactly the right thing to say. You did it.
opts.say: Mind went blank—just felt exhausted and empty for weeks.

opts.t: Talk about work instead: “Work's been really busy, so I've mostly been dealing with logistics…”
opts.why: Performing competence wastes safe space.
opts.re: How did it go? …You can tell me the real part.

opts.t: Look down at your hands: “Honestly, I'm fine. I don't know why I'm here.”
opts.why: Gazing downward maintains blockades.
opts.re: …It's okay if it was hard. First times are.

rooms.title: Doctor's Office Symptoms
rooms.scene: It's your intake checkup with the doctor.

opts.t: Be straightforward: “Sleep is broken, appetite gone, mood flat for a month.”
opts.why: Physical symptoms help doctors give proper care.
opts.re: You told them everything. That's how they can help.
opts.say: Sleep is broken, appetite gone, mood flat for a month.

opts.t: Keep it simple: “Mostly I just can't sleep. Otherwise I'm okay.”
opts.why: Treating one symptom leaves depression unaddressed.
opts.re: Did you tell them about the low mood too?

opts.t: Nod along: “Everything's fine, I think. Just a routine checkup.”
opts.why: Saying everything is fine hides the symptoms the doctor needs to hear about.
opts.re: …How did the checkup go?

rooms.title: Wrong Therapist Fit
rooms.scene: You realize your therapist isn't a good fit.

opts.t: “Fit matters—keeping slot while reaching out to others.”
opts.why: Treating selection like specialists prevents quitting.
opts.re: Fit matters. I'm proud of you for speaking up for yourself.
opts.say: Fit matters—keeping slot while reaching out to others.

opts.t: Stay put to be polite: “I'll keep going for six months. I don't want to hurt their feelings.”
opts.why: People-pleasing stalls healing.
opts.re: You don't owe anyone six months if it's not working.

opts.t: Close the booking page: “Therapy just doesn't work for me.”
opts.why: Closing portal tabs halts care management.
opts.re: …Do you want help finding someone else?

rooms.title: Medication Side Effects
rooms.scene: You feel groggy from your new prescription.

opts.t: Message prescriber: “Feeling groggy—should I adjust safely?”
opts.why: Collaborating prevents abrupt discontinuation.
opts.re: Good call asking first. You're taking care of yourself.
opts.say: Feeling groggy—should I adjust safely?

opts.t: Adjust it yourself: “I'll just cut the pills in half. That should fix it.”
opts.why: Self-adjusting risks rebound symptoms.
opts.re: Maybe ask the doctor before cutting them?

opts.t: Leave the bottle on the shelf: “Maybe I'll just stop taking them.”
opts.why: Leaving bottles untouched bypasses consultation.
opts.re: …How are you feeling on the new meds?

rooms.title: A Support Group
rooms.scene: Your counselor suggests a weekly support group for people going through something similar.

opts.t: “That sounds scary, but maybe hearing from others would help. I'll try one session.”
opts.why: Trying something once, despite nerves, can show you that you're not alone.
opts.re: One session is a great start. I'll drive you if you want.

opts.t: “Maybe later. I'll try it once I'm feeling better.”
opts.why: Waiting until you feel better can mean missing the support that would help you get there.
opts.re: Maybe it could help you feel better sooner?

opts.t: “A room full of sad people? That would make me worse.”
opts.why: Writing it off before trying closes a door to people who truly understand.
opts.re: You won't know until you try. I can go with you.

rooms.title: Being Kind to Yourself
rooms.scene: You keep replaying a mistake from work.

opts.t: Go for a walk: “It was one mistake. I'd tell a friend that's okay—so it's okay for me too.”
opts.why: Self-compassion helps you recover faster.
opts.re: There you go. Talk to yourself like you'd talk to me.

opts.t: “Give me twenty minutes to dissect where focus slipped.”
opts.why: Rumination traps you in self-punishment.
opts.re: Okay… but please don't be too hard on yourself.
opts.say: Give me twenty minutes to dissect where focus slipped.

opts.t: Stare at the spreadsheet: “How could I be so stupid? I'm going to check every single line.”
opts.why: Staring at work reinforces obsessive error review.
opts.re: …It's late. One mistake isn't who you are.

rooms.title: Encouraging Helper to Rest
rooms.scene: {P} looks exhausted after caring for you all week.

opts.t: “You matter too. See friends—I'll call my sister.”
opts.why: Shared support protects you both.
opts.re: …Really? Thank you. I think I do need that weekend.
opts.say: You matter too. See friends—I'll call my sister.

opts.t: Make a silent promise: “From now on, I'll keep the heavy days to myself.”
opts.why: Going silent leaves you isolated.
opts.re: …You've gone quiet. Please keep telling me the hard stuff.

opts.t: Turn off the light: “Go to bed. I'm clearly wearing you out.”
opts.why: Calling yourself a burden turns their tiredness into proof against you.
opts.re: …Oh. Lights off. Okay, goodnight.

rooms.title: Catching All-or-Nothing Thinking
rooms.scene: You ate takeout for dinner again, and your brain whispers 'failure'.

opts.t: Reframe: “Fed myself, got through—normal maintenance day.”
opts.why: Replacing binary grading stops spirals.
opts.re: Fed yourself and got through. That's a win.
opts.say: Fed myself, got through—normal maintenance day.

opts.t: Set an early alarm: “I'll get up at 5 tomorrow to make up for being lazy.”
opts.why: Punitive compensation treats rest as debt.
opts.re: You don't have to earn rest. Sleep in if you need it.

opts.t: Toss the takeout box: “Can't even cook a meal. Pathetic.”
opts.why: Calling yourself pathetic over a takeout meal feeds the inner critic.
opts.re: …You okay? You went quiet.

rooms.title: Social Media Comparison
rooms.scene: You're scrolling your phone, seeing everyone's milestones.

opts.t: Set phone across room: “Comparing struggle to highlight reels.”
opts.why: Naming illusions protects self-esteem.
opts.re: Good move. Highlight reels aren't real life.
opts.say: I'm comparing my struggle to everyone's highlight reels.

opts.t: Keep scrolling and commenting: “So happy for you!! Amazing news!!”
opts.why: Performing cheerfulness deepens dissonance.
opts.re: You seem drained. Want to put the phone down for a bit?

opts.t: Tap to the next story: “Everyone's moving forward except me.”
opts.why: Advancing posts deepens comparison loops.
opts.re: …Hey. Come sit with me instead?

rooms.title: Forgiving Yourself for Snapping
rooms.scene: You feel guilty for snapping at {p} earlier.

opts.t: Apologize simply: “Sorry I was short, overwhelmed not mad.”
opts.why: Clean accountability restores connection.
opts.re: Thank you. I know you were overwhelmed. We're okay.
opts.say: Sorry I was short, overwhelmed not mad.

opts.t: Keep apologizing: “I'm so sorry. Really. I'm sorry. Are you mad? I'm sorry.”
opts.why: Excessive punishment forces partner to comfort.
opts.re: You've said sorry enough. I really am okay.

opts.t: Turn to face the wall: “Just leave me alone. I'll only make it worse.”
opts.why: Turning back maintains isolation.
opts.re: …Can we talk? I'm not mad.

rooms.title: Lowering Bar on Hard Days
rooms.scene: You have zero energy today.

opts.t: Do the bare minimum: “Water, crackers, wash my face. That counts as a win today.”
opts.why: Scaling care keeps dignity intact.
opts.re: Water, crackers, a clean face — that's a win. I'm proud of you.

opts.t: Start cleaning anyway: “If I deep-clean the whole house, I'll feel productive.”
opts.why: Ignoring exhaustion leads to crashes.
opts.re: Please sit down. The cleaning can wait.

opts.t: Leave the dishes: “What's the point. They'll just pile up again.”
opts.why: Leaving items unaddressed reinforces guilt.
opts.re: …I'll get the dishes. Go rest.

rooms.title: Boundaries with Unhelpful Advice
rooms.scene: A relative gives you unhelpful advice about your mood.

opts.t: Smile, pivot: “Glad that helped—working with my doctor. Garden doing well?”
opts.why: Polite deflection saves energy.
opts.re: Smooth! You protected your energy — nicely done.
opts.say: Glad that helped—working with my doctor. Garden doing well?

opts.t: Start a long explanation: “Actually, depression is about neurotransmitters, so let me explain…”
opts.why: Debating drains scarce energy.
opts.re: You don't have to win that argument. Save your energy.

opts.t: Nod once: “Yeah. Maybe you're right. I should just try harder.”
opts.why: Agreeing that you just need to try harder absorbs a harmful idea about depression.
opts.re: …You okay after that conversation?

rooms.title: Nothing Left to Give
rooms.scene: Bedtime exhaustion.
rooms.ask: How do you close the night?

opts.t: “At zero percent—plugging in phone, resting early. Love you.”
opts.why: Honest communication prevents misunderstandings.
opts.re: Rest well. Love you too. Thank you for telling me.
opts.say: At zero percent—plugging in phone, resting early. Love you.

opts.t: Stay on the couch: “I'll just sit here a bit longer. I'm not even tired.”
opts.why: Forcing presence delays needed rest.
opts.re: You look exhausted… go to bed, I promise it's okay.

opts.t: Switch off the lamp: “Night.”
opts.why: A one-word goodnight hides how empty you feel and leaves you alone with it.
opts.re: …Goodnight. I'm right here.

rooms.title: Protecting Sleep During Stress
rooms.scene: Deadlines are piling up this week.

opts.t: Set alarm: “Week is intense, guarding bedtime and counseling slot.”
opts.why: Protecting anchors stops stress from becoming setbacks.
opts.re: Guarding your sleep and your session — that's so smart.
opts.say: Week is intense, guarding bedtime and counseling slot.

opts.t: Plan to push through: “Four hours of sleep is fine for one week.”
opts.why: Sleep debt destabilizes mood.
opts.re: Four hours? Please don't. You matter more than the deadline.

opts.t: Leave the laptop open: “Sleep can wait. Deadlines can't.”
opts.why: Leaving workstations illuminated invites overworking.
opts.re: …Want me to close that for you?

rooms.title: Returning to Hobby Slowly
rooms.scene: Your old instrument feels rusty in your hands.

opts.t: “Five messy minutes—zero expectation to be good today.”
opts.why: Separating enjoyment from performance restores soothing.
opts.re: Five messy minutes! I loved hearing it again.
opts.say: Five messy minutes—zero expectation to be good today.

opts.t: Practice for an hour: “I used to be good at this. I'm not stopping until I'm back to that level.”
opts.why: Demanding peak performance turns hobbies into chores.
opts.re: An hour is a lot. It's okay to play badly.

opts.t: Put it back on the shelf: “I've forgotten everything. What's the point.”
opts.why: Returning items to storage abandons attempts.
opts.re: …You'll pick it up again when you're ready.

rooms.title: The hardest night
rooms.scene: Late at night, the dark thoughts are loud. {P} knocks and asks to come in.

opts.t: “Having dark thoughts. I'm scared.”
opts.why: Telling someone is the bravest act; you aren't alone.
opts.re: Thank you for telling me. I'm right here. You're not alone.
opts.say: Having dark thoughts. I'm scared.

opts.t: “Thanks for coming in—my mind is racing.”
opts.why: Softening truth keeps you from safety support.
opts.re: I'm here. But it feels like more than racing thoughts… please tell me.
opts.say: Thanks for coming in—my mind is racing.

opts.t: Face the wall: “I'm trying to sleep. Can we talk tomorrow?”
opts.why: Putting it off until tomorrow blocks the support you need right now.
opts.re: …Are you awake? I'll stay right outside the door.

rooms.title: Reaching Out When Alone
rooms.scene: It's 1:00 AM and you're spiraling alone.

opts.t: Text/call crisis line (988): “Not in safe headspace—stay on line?”
opts.why: Reaching out interrupts isolation.
opts.re: You reached out. That was so brave. I'm coming to sit with you too.
opts.say: Not in safe headspace—stay on line?

opts.t: Wait it out: “I'll give it two hours. Maybe it'll pass on its own.”
opts.why: Waiting alone increases risk.
opts.re: Please don't wait alone. Call now — or wake me. Always.

opts.t: Put your phone face down: “No one's awake anyway. I'll just deal with it.”
opts.why: Placing devices face down seals off help.
opts.re: …I woke up. Can I come in? Please talk to me.

rooms.title: Writing Goodbyes
rooms.scene: Late at night, you notice you've been writing goodbye messages in your head. {P} knocks softly.
rooms.line: I saw your light on. Are you okay?

opts.t: Let {them} in: “No. I've been having thoughts of not being here. I'm scared.”
opts.why: Saying it out loud is the bravest and most important step. You don't have to carry it alone.
opts.re: Thank you for telling me. I'm right here. We're going to get help together.

opts.t: “Just can't sleep. Lots on my mind tonight.”
opts.why: Softening the truth means they can't help with what's really happening.
opts.re: …It feels like more than that. Please tell me.

opts.t: “I'm fine. Turn the light off when you go.”
opts.why: Sending them away keeps you alone with the most dangerous thoughts.
opts.re: …I'll be right outside. Please call me if anything changes.

rooms.title: They'd Be Better Off
rooms.scene: After an argument with yourself all evening, one thought keeps repeating: everyone would be better off without you.
rooms.ask: What do you do with that thought?

opts.t: Go to {p}: “My brain keeps telling me you'd all be better off without me. I need help.”
opts.why: That thought is a symptom, not the truth. Telling someone breaks its power.
opts.re: We would never be better off without you. Never. Let's get help right now.

opts.t: Tell yourself: “It's just a thought. I'll sleep it off and see how I feel tomorrow.”
opts.why: Hoping it passes alone leaves you without support while the thought is loud.
opts.re: You seem really far away tonight. Talk to me?

opts.t: Start believing it: “Maybe it's true. Maybe I'm just in the way.”
opts.why: Agreeing with the thought lets it grow. This is the moment to reach out.
opts.re: Hey… you're not in the way. Please come talk to me.

rooms.title: Giving Things Away
rooms.scene: You've quietly given your favorite jacket to {p}. {They} hold{s} it, looking worried.
rooms.line: Why are you giving me this? You love this jacket.

opts.t: Tell the truth: “Because I've been thinking about not being around. I'm scared of how much.”
opts.why: Giving things away can be a warning sign. Being honest lets them help you stay safe.
opts.re: Thank you for being honest. I'm not leaving your side. Let's call for help now.

opts.t: “I just don't wear it anymore. It looks better on you.”
opts.why: A cover story hides a warning sign from the person who could help.
opts.re: …Are you sure? You've been giving a lot of things away lately.

opts.t: “Can you not make a big deal out of everything?”
opts.why: Snapping shuts down the exact question that could keep you safe.
opts.re: I'm asking because I love you. Please talk to me.

rooms.title: Choosing Safety Over Secrecy
rooms.scene: {P} gently asks if you're having thoughts of ending your life.

opts.t: Answer honestly: “Yes… sometimes I have those thoughts. Can we call a crisis line together right now?”
opts.why: Honesty lets loved ones help you stay safe.
opts.re: Thank you for being honest. Let's call together right now. I'm not leaving.

opts.t: “Thoughts cross my mind, but I'll sleep it off.”
opts.why: Postponing help leaves you alone with acute risk.
opts.re: I hear you. I'm not leaving you alone tonight — let's call someone now.
opts.say: Thoughts cross my mind, but I'll sleep it off.

opts.t: Squeeze {their} hand: “I'm fine. Please don't make this a big thing.”
opts.why: Asking them not to make it “a big thing” keeps you in danger. This needs help now.
opts.re: I love you too much to pretend that's fine. Let's call someone together.

rooms.title: Calling Together
rooms.scene: {P} has the crisis line number ready, but your hands are shaking.
rooms.line: I can dial. You don't have to say it perfectly.

opts.t: Nod: “Okay. You dial. Stay next to me while I talk.”
opts.why: Accepting help to make the call keeps you connected to support right when you need it.
opts.re: I'm right here. You're doing so well. Just say what you can.

opts.t: “Maybe I'll text them instead… later.”
opts.why: Texting is fine, but putting it off until later leaves the danger unaddressed.
opts.re: Texting is okay—but let's do it right now, together.

opts.t: “Please don't. I'm not calling anyone.”
opts.why: Refusing help in a crisis keeps you alone with the danger.
opts.re: I love you too much to do nothing. I'm calling them with you.

rooms.title: Not Alone Tonight
rooms.scene: After talking for a while, {p} pulls a blanket over to the chair beside your bed.
rooms.line: I'm going to stay with you tonight. Is that okay?

opts.t: “Yes. Please stay. I don't want to be alone right now.”
opts.why: Accepting company during a crisis is one of the simplest ways to stay safe.
opts.re: I'm not going anywhere. We'll take it one hour at a time.

opts.t: “You don't have to. Really. I'll be okay on my own.”
opts.why: Turning down company out of guilt can leave you alone when the thoughts return.
opts.re: I want to. I'll be right here in the chair.

opts.t: “I just want to be alone. Please go.”
opts.why: Being alone tonight can make dangerous thoughts much louder.
opts.re: I'll leave the door open and stay right outside. I'm not going far.

rooms.title: Making the Space Safe
rooms.scene: {P} gently asks if {they} can put away your medications and anything else you might use to hurt yourself, just for now.

opts.t: “Okay. I think that's a good idea. Thank you for helping me stay safe.”
opts.why: Putting dangerous things out of reach during a crisis is one of the most effective ways to stay safe.
opts.re: Thank you for trusting me. We'll keep everything safe together.

opts.t: “Fine… but give them back tomorrow, okay?”
opts.why: Agreeing helps tonight, but rushing it back may come too soon.
opts.re: Let's ask your doctor when it's the right time.

opts.t: “You're treating me like a child. Leave my things alone.”
opts.why: Refusing safety steps out of pride keeps the danger close.
opts.re: I'm not trying to control you. I just want you here tomorrow.

rooms.title: The Morning After
rooms.scene: It's the morning after the hardest night. You're exhausted, but safe.
rooms.line: How are you feeling this morning?

opts.t: “Tired, but here. Can you help me call my doctor today and make a safety plan?”
opts.why: Following up with professional care the next day turns one hard night into a plan for staying safe.
opts.re: Yes. Let's call right after breakfast. I'm so glad you're here.

opts.t: “Better, I think. Let's just pretend last night didn't happen.”
opts.why: Moving on without follow-up leaves you without a plan if the thoughts come back.
opts.re: I'm glad you're better. But let's still call your doctor today.

opts.t: “Fine. It was nothing. I overreacted.”
opts.why: Downplaying a crisis can stop you from getting the care you need.
opts.re: It wasn't nothing. You were really hurting, and that matters.

setbacks.title: Waking Up Heavy Again
setbacks.scene: After some good days, you wake up heavy again.

opts.t: “Bad day, not bad life. Can you sit for a bit?”
opts.why: Treating bad days as normal stops shame spirals.
opts.re: Bad day, not a bad life. Move over — I'm staying.
opts.say: Bad day, not bad life. Can you sit for a bit?

opts.t: “Slow start, give me ten minutes and I'll force myself.”
opts.why: Masking drains remaining energy.
opts.re: You don't have to force it. It's okay to go slow today.
opts.say: Slow start, give me ten minutes and I'll force myself.

opts.t: Pull the blanket up: “Just leave me. Today's a write-off.”
opts.why: Pulling bedding upward closes interaction.
opts.re: …I'll be right here when you're ready.

setbacks.title: After Missing Counseling
setbacks.scene: You missed your counseling session, and the clinic called.

opts.t: “I panicked. Sit with me while I reschedule?”
opts.why: Honesty and small steps keep momentum alive.
opts.re: Of course. Let's call them together right now.
opts.say: I panicked. Sit with me while I reschedule?

opts.t: “Work ran into it, I'll catch them next month.”
opts.why: Practical excuses delay getting back on track.
opts.re: …Was it really work? It's okay if you got scared.
opts.say: Work ran into it, I'll catch them next month.

opts.t: Put your phone on the charger: “Doesn't matter. I'll deal with it later.”
opts.why: Plugging in phones ignores inquiry.
opts.re: …Want to talk about what happened?
